 Print India's Shubman Gill and Rishabh Pant (AP/PTI) Shubman Gill and Rishabh Pant etched their names in the record books during India's first Test against New Zealand at the Basin Reserve in Wellington, becoming the first two Indian batters to cross the 3,000-run mark in the ICC World Test Championship (WTC). Gill was the first to reach the landmark on Saturday, achieving the feat during a commanding innings of 98 on Day 3 of the opening Test. Pant followed him later in the day, becoming the second Indian to enter the exclusive club. He also created history by becoming the first wicketkeeper in the world to score 3,000 runs in the WTC. Watch KL Rahul opens up on his preparation, century and India's plans against New Zealand Having accumulated 2,917 runs in 76 innings before the Wellington Test, Gill needed 83 more to reach the milestone. The India captain got there in style, clearing the boundary off Glenn Phillips for a six in the 115th over during the third session. He went on to make 98 before Jacob Duffy bowled him on the third-last delivery of the day's play, leaving him just two runs short of a century. Pant, meanwhile, had 2,948 WTC runs heading into the contest and required another 52 to reach the 3,000-run mark. The wicketkeeper-batter completed the milestone with a boundary in the 123rd over, an effort that also brought up his 22nd Test half-century. He remained unbeaten on 55 off 62 deliveries at stumps. Interestingly, Gill's achievement also continued a sequence of Indian batters reaching successive WTC run milestones. Ajinkya Rahane was the first Indian to register 1,000 runs in the championship, followed by Rohit Sharma, who became the first to reach 2,000. Gill has now become the first Indian to breach the 3,000-run barrier. Join conversation

 India's batting dominance on Day 3 
 The milestones came during a prolific batting effort from India, who finished Day 3 at 486/4, establishing a lead of 118 runs over New Zealand's first-innings total of 368. KL Rahul headlined the effort with a magnificent 136, becoming the first Indian opener to score Test centuries in all four SENA countries - South Africa, England, New Zealand and Australia. Yashasvi Jaiswal had laid the foundation with an 85 on Day 2, while Devdutt Padikkal chipped in with 80. It was also the first time India's top five batters had all registered scores of at least 50 in the same Test innings outside India. With Pant unbeaten alongside nightwatchman Anshul Kamboj, who was on nought after negotiating the final two deliveries, India ended the day firmly in control of the contest.
